subject.title: [Feature]: Add optional capability descriptors to tool definitions

question: What canonical tool-capability descriptor taxonomy and trust semantics should OpenClaw expose to plugin policy and audit consumers?
rationale: This turns tool metadata into public security-policy input and overlaps multiple open capability/provenance proposals, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent SDK/Gateway contract.

options.title: Approve Unified Descriptor Contract
options.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics, thread them through tool definitions, plugin metadata, inventory, Gateway protocol, and hook events, and document that declarations do not bypass host policy.

options.title: Fold Into Permissions Work
options.body: Keep this blocked behind the broader capability-permission/default-deny model so descriptors ship only as part of an enforceable grant system.

options.title: Limit To Security Matrix
options.body: Use the Security Matrix audit model as the canonical consumer and avoid a general public descriptor field until that implementation lands and owners approve the vocabulary.

recommendation.title: Approve Unified Descriptor Contract
recommendation.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics, thread them through tool definitions, plugin metadata, inventory, Gateway protocol, and hook events, and document that declarations do not bypass host policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged host-hook foundation owns the closest SDK seam for trusted policies and plugin tool metadata.
